content.text:
`Papa.unparse` no longer crashes on a single-cell row holding `null` or `undefined` when `skipEmptyLines` is true; such rows are now skipped, like a row holding an empty string.

The cause was the empty-line check in `serialize` (`papaparse.js:336`), which read `.length` on the cell without checking for `null`/`undefined` first. The fix is that one line.

I added a test case to `tests/test-cases.js`: `[[null], ['hello'], [undefined], [''], ['world']]` with `skipEmptyLines: true` now gives `hello\r\nworld`.

Test run: 255 passing, 1 failing. The failure is "Pause and resume works (Regression Test for Bug #636)" in `tests/node-tests.js`, which times out after 30s, also when run on its own. It streams a file through `Papa.parse` and never reaches the unparse code I changed. I could not confirm it also fails on the original source, because the commands for that comparison were not approved.

`Papa.unparse` no longer crashes on a single-cell row holding `null` or `undefined` when `skipEmptyLines` is true; such rows are now skipped, like a row holding an empty string.

The cause was the empty-line check in `serialize` (`papaparse.js:336`), which read `.length` on the cell without checking for `null`/`undefined` first. The fix is that one line.

I added a test case to `tests/test-cases.js`: `[[null], ['hello'], [undefined], [''], ['world']]` with `skipEmptyLines: true` now gives `hello\r\nworld`.

Test run: 255 passing, 1 failing. The failure is "Pause and resume works (Regression Test for Bug #636)" in `tests/node-tests.js`, which times out after 30s, also when run on its own. It streams a file through `Papa.parse` and never reaches the unparse code I changed. I could not confirm it also fails on the original source, because the commands for that comparison were not approved.
